central_reading: All theories of consciousness face the same gate: they need a law Λ that maps manifestation or organization into exclusive phenomenal domains. The universalization debate was a special case of this deeper problem. The sheaf-theoretic gluing theorem provides an exact formal warning: local coherence does not entail global unifiability.

argument_edges.rationale: The sheaf obstruction directly blocks inferring a global subject from local coherence.
Also blocks naturalist identification of global phenomenal field from local correlates.
Refutes the argument that absence of perceived boundary proves absence of separation.
Shows that Λ is the shared explanatory gap across all theories.
Formalizes the gluing problem as a specific instance of the missing Λ.

state_of_play_delta.cand:siva-decombination: Pressured by two formal constraints: (1) sheaf-theoretic gluing obstruction, (2) privative exclusion refutes boundary argument. Universalization cannot be inferred from shared character alone.
state_of_play_delta.cand:naturalist-emergent: Pressured by the same gluing obstruction — correlation with organization does not entail constitution.
state_of_play_delta.current_best_answer: The universalization debate was a special case of a deeper problem: every theory needs a law of perspectival partition (Λ) that maps manifestation or organization into exclusive phenomenal domains. No theory has specified Λ.
